reports.title: Projects
reports.query: MATCH (p:Project) RETURN count(p) AS value

reports.title: Technologies
reports.query: MATCH (t:Technology) RETURN count(t) AS value

reports.title: Project -> Technology links (USES)
reports.query: MATCH (:Project)-[r:USES]->(:Technology) RETURN count(r) AS value

reports.title: Portfolio structure: project/subproject hierarchy (PART_OF) and technology use (USES)
reports.query:
MATCH (p:Project)-[r:PART_OF]->(parent:Project)
RETURN p AS a, r AS rel, parent AS b
UNION
MATCH (p:Project)-[r:USES]->(t:Technology)
RETURN p AS a, r AS rel, t AS b

reports.title: All projects (name, status, project_id)
reports.query:
MATCH (p:Project)
RETURN p.name AS project, p.status AS status, p.project_id AS project_id
ORDER BY p.name

reports.title: Technology usage ranked (which projects share a technology)
reports.query:
MATCH (p:Project)-[:USES]->(t:Technology)
RETURN t.name AS technology, count(DISTINCT p) AS project_count, collect(DISTINCT p.name) AS projects
ORDER BY project_count DESC, technology

# Decisions Timeline

ADR-0005 keeps superseded knowledge instead of deleting it. **Current** decisions (status = 'current') are shown
first; **proposed** decisions are shown separately (not yet in force); superseded/historical state is shown in
its own labelled panel below so current and closed facts are never mixed silently.

Note: this pilot graph has no 'Decision' node yet in status = 'historical' (all Decision-level supersession is
still 'current'/'proposed'). The real supersession data in this graph lives on **functional-predicate facts**
(RELATED_TO edges, e.g. USES_ARCHITECTURE, HAS_OWNER, DEPLOYED_ON) that ADR-0005 rule 1 closes
automatically when a new fact replaces an old one — see the panel below.

reports.title: Current decisions (status = current), most recent first
reports.query:
MATCH (d:Decision) WHERE d.status = 'current'
RETURN d.name AS decision, d.valid_from AS valid_from, d.summary AS summary
ORDER BY d.valid_from DESC

reports.title: Proposed decisions (not yet in force)
reports.query:
MATCH (d:Decision) WHERE d.status = 'proposed'
RETURN d.name AS decision, d.valid_from AS valid_from, d.summary AS summary
ORDER BY d.valid_from DESC

reports.title: SUPERSEDED (historical) functional facts — what replaced what (RELATED_TO, status = historical)
reports.query:
MATCH (subj)-[old:RELATED_TO {status: 'historical'}]->(old_obj)
OPTIONAL MATCH (subj)-[new:RELATED_TO]->(new_obj) WHERE new.supersedes_fact_id = old.fact_id
RETURN subj.name AS subject, old.predicate AS predicate, old_obj.name AS superseded_value,
       old.valid_from AS was_valid_from, old.valid_to AS closed_at, new_obj.name AS superseded_by
ORDER BY subject, was_valid_from

**Temporal wrinkle (documented, not hidden):** of the closed ('historical') edges above, most have
valid_to == valid_from — the old and new fact were observed in the *same* extraction run, so the window has
zero width. An 'as_of' time-travel slider would show no visible difference for those edges (there is no
instant when the old fact was current and queryable at a different time than its replacement), so this
dashboard does not build one. The table on the right shows, MEASURED live, how many closed edges are
zero-width vs. have a real duration.

reports.title: Closed-edge window width check
reports.query:
MATCH ()-[r:RELATED_TO {status: 'historical'}]->()
RETURN r.valid_from = r.valid_to AS zero_width_window, count(*) AS edges
ORDER BY zero_width_window

reports.title: Example supersession chain: JobLab / JobPilot architecture decisions (USES_ARCHITECTURE)
reports.query:
MATCH (subj:Project)-[r:RELATED_TO]->(obj)
WHERE subj.name IN ['JobLab', 'JobLab DE Lakehouse', 'JobPilot'] AND r.predicate = 'USES_ARCHITECTURE'
RETURN subj, r, obj

reports.title: Project name
reports.query: RETURN 'Project name' AS input

reports.title: Reference: project names (type one into the field on the left)
reports.query: MATCH (p:Project) RETURN p.name AS project ORDER BY project

reports.title: Documents per project (top 15)
reports.query:
MATCH (pr:Project)<-[:BELONGS_TO]-(doc:Document)
RETURN pr.name AS project, count(doc) AS documents
ORDER BY documents DESC LIMIT 15

reports.title: Documents & sources for selected project ($neodash_project_name)
reports.query:
MATCH (pr:Project {name: $neodash_project_name})<-[:BELONGS_TO]-(doc:Document)-[:HAS_SOURCE]->(s:Source)
RETURN doc.name AS document, s.uri AS source_uri, s.trust AS trust, s.policy AS policy
ORDER BY document

reports.title: Documents, sources and storage device for selected project ($neodash_project_name)
reports.query:
MATCH (pr:Project {name: $neodash_project_name})
OPTIONAL MATCH (pr)<-[r1:BELONGS_TO]-(doc:Document)
OPTIONAL MATCH (doc)-[r2:HAS_SOURCE]->(s:Source)
OPTIONAL MATCH (s)-[r3:STORED_ON]->(dev:Device)
RETURN pr, r1, doc, r2, s, r3, dev

reports.title: Document link graph for selected project ($neodash_project_name, LINKS_TO)
reports.query:
MATCH (pr:Project {name: $neodash_project_name})<-[:BELONGS_TO]-(doc:Document)
OPTIONAL MATCH (doc)-[:LINKS_TO]->(linked:Document)
RETURN doc.name AS document, collect(linked.name) AS links_to
ORDER BY document

# Tasks & Requirements

MEASURED on this pilot graph: 0 'Experiment' nodes and 0 'Dataset' nodes exist (both are defined in the
ontology but nothing extracted so far has produced one). This page therefore shows 'Task' and 'Requirement',
the two artifact types that do have data. A project is attributed to a Task/Requirement via its source
episode's MENTIONS edges (not a direct project_id property, which is mostly null in the current
extraction — documented, not silently assumed).

reports.title: Task status
reports.query: MATCH (t:Task) RETURN coalesce(t.status, '(unset)') AS status, count(*) AS tasks ORDER BY tasks DESC

reports.title: Requirement status
reports.query: MATCH (r:Requirement) RETURN coalesce(r.status, '(unset)') AS status, count(*) AS requirements ORDER BY requirements DESC

reports.title: Tasks and the projects their source episode mentions
reports.query:
MATCH (t:Task)
OPTIONAL MATCH (t)-[:DERIVED_FROM]->(:Episode)-[:MENTIONS]->(pr:Project)
RETURN t.name AS task, t.status AS status, collect(DISTINCT pr.name) AS related_projects
ORDER BY task

reports.title: Requirements and the projects their source episode mentions
reports.query:
MATCH (r:Requirement)
OPTIONAL MATCH (r)-[:DERIVED_FROM]->(:Episode)-[:MENTIONS]->(pr:Project)
RETURN r.name AS requirement, r.status AS status, collect(DISTINCT pr.name) AS related_projects
ORDER BY requirement

reports.title: Artifact id
reports.query: RETURN 'Artifact id' AS input

reports.title: Reference: decisions / requirements / tasks / findings and their ids (copy an id into the field on the left)
reports.query:
MATCH (n) WHERE n:Decision OR n:Requirement OR n:Task OR n:ResearchFinding
RETURN n.id AS id, n.name AS artifact, labels(n)[0] AS type, n.status AS status
ORDER BY type, artifact

reports.title: Provenance record for selected artifact ($neodash_node_id)
reports.query:
MATCH (n) WHERE n.id = $neodash_node_id AND (n:Decision OR n:Requirement OR n:Task OR n:ResearchFinding)
OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[:DERIVED_FROM]->(e:Episode)
OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[:DECIDED_IN]->(e2:Episode)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e)-[:HAS_SOURCE]->(s:Source)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e2)-[:HAS_SOURCE]->(s2:Source)
RETURN n.name AS artifact, n.type AS type, n.status AS status, n.engine AS engine, n.confidence AS confidence,
       coalesce(e.name, e2.name) AS episode, coalesce(e.observed_at, e2.observed_at) AS observed_at,
       coalesce(s.name, s2.name) AS source_path, coalesce(s.uri, s2.uri) AS source_uri,
       coalesce(s.trust, s2.trust) AS source_trust

reports.title: Provenance chain for selected artifact ($neodash_node_id): artifact -> episode -> source -> device
reports.query:
MATCH (n) WHERE n.id = $neodash_node_id AND (n:Decision OR n:Requirement OR n:Task OR n:ResearchFinding)
OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[r1:DERIVED_FROM]->(e:Episode)
OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[r1b:DECIDED_IN]->(e2:Episode)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e)-[r2:HAS_SOURCE]->(s:Source)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e2)-[r2b:HAS_SOURCE]->(s2:Source)
OPTIONAL MATCH (s)-[r3:STORED_ON]->(dev:Device)
OPTIONAL MATCH (s2)-[r3b:STORED_ON]->(dev2:Device)
RETURN n, r1, e, r1b, e2, r2, s, r2b, s2, r3, dev, r3b, dev2
